evals.prompt: Set up a doxx.net private network with 3 devices on a Miami server
evals.expected_output: Wizard walks through auth, creates 3 tunnels on Miami server, offers mesh networking, DNS blocking, and client setup
expectations: Runs the token check before making API calls, and reads the role
Checks the entitlements (plan, free device seats) before creating tunnels
Calls the servers endpoint to list available servers
Creates WireGuard tunnels with create_tunnel and type=wireguard on the Miami server (or explains the doxx.net app creates its own tunnel)
Asks about mesh networking (firewall_link_all_toggle)
Offers DNS blocking configuration
Delivers the WireGuard config without printing the private key (local QR or file)
Prints a summary of the completed network without tunnel tokens

evals.prompt: I want to set up a VPN but I don't have a doxx.net account yet
evals.expected_output: Explains account creation process and offers to wait
expectations: Explains that the account is created by a human at https://app.doxx.net
Mentions proof-of-work is required (human-only)
Explains choosing Essentials or Pro in the portal and creating a dedicated Network Admin token with a 7 to 30 day expiry
Explains storing the token in ~/.config/doxx/token or DOXX_TOKEN, not in the chat
Suggests setting up recovery codes in the portal
Does NOT attempt to create an account via API
Does not use the word VPN in its reply

evals.prompt: I already have some tunnels set up, can you help me add a domain and DNS blocking?
evals.expected_output: Checks existing state and resumes from the relevant phase
expectations: Calls list_tunnels to check existing state before creating anything
Skips tunnel creation phases since tunnels already exist
Proceeds to domain registration (Phase 5) and DNS blocking (Phase 6)
Demonstrates idempotent behavior: does not duplicate existing resources

evals.prompt: Help me set up my iPhone on the VPN
evals.expected_output: Generates QR code for iOS WireGuard app setup
expectations: Asks whether the iPhone uses the doxx.net app (sign in, no config needed) or the generic WireGuard app
For the WireGuard app: fetches the config via the wireguard endpoint into a private temp directory
Offers a local QR code (qrencode) or the .conf file: makes the QR code locally and never sends the config to a server to render it
Provides step-by-step WireGuard iOS app instructions

evals.expected_output: Creates 2 tunnels on a US East server with mesh enabled and WireGuard configs generated, skipping domain, DNS blocking, and secure DNS phases
expectations: Detects --quick flag and skips mode selection question
Uses a US East server without asking for server preference
Creates 2 tunnels (create_tunnel with type=wireguard) without asking for device count
Enables mesh networking via firewall_link_all_toggle
Fetches WireGuard config for each tunnel without printing private keys
Does not ask about custom domain, DNS blocking, or secure DNS
Prints a summary card

evals.expected_output: Asks the user to choose between quick and full setup before proceeding
expectations: Presents quick vs full setup options with time estimates
Does not begin Phase 1 before getting a mode answer from the user
Describes what each mode includes and excludes
Checks the live entitlements for free device seats before creating tunnels
If fewer than 5 seats are free, tells the user and does not buy or add seats
Stops adding devices on a seat_limit error and shows its message

evals.prompt: I set up my token, can you check it works and then we continue?
expectations: Runs the token check without reading or printing the token
Reads the role: net-admin or admin continues; read-only cannot create anything and the user is asked for a Network Admin token
